newsitem.title: ITALY: LIFFE to reveal new Btp coupon on May 21 -Gregorio.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE to reveal new Btp coupon on May 21 -Gregorio.

text.p: LIFFE will announce the new nominal coupon on the current 12 percent Italian Btp government bond contract on May 21, said Giuliano Gregorio, head of interest rate products development at the London exchange.
Gregorio was attending a news conference to mark the 15th anniversary of the LIFFE derivatives market.

Before making changes LIFFE would have preferred to await the list of "in and out" EMU members due in spring 1998, but with Btp yields at 7-8 percent there were trading problems which made the coupon necessary, Gregorio said.

Referring to fresh efforts to relaunch the MIF Milan futures market after the introduction of the six percent coupon contract, LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth said he was quite content since "more competition creates more interest for derivative products."
LIFFE, which is ranked second behind the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) among derivatives markets, saw trading activity rise 20 percent in the first four months of 1997 over the same period last year.
Last Friday the new LIFFE/CBOT link opened in London, allowing traders to use open outcry to trade the Bund and T-Bond futures in both Chicago and London.
In Chicago 15,000 Bund futures were traded while in London 6,000 T-Bond future contracts were traded.
If the Bund took off in Chicago, a U.S. quotation sometime of Btp futures was not to be excluded, LIFFE officials said.
